method: Static first reasoned review: atomscan slow scans and cleave facts for all original paths; rizin, pefile, Capstone and Go objdump on native entry paths and carved PEs. No sample or embedded program was executed.

samples.identification: Eclipse platform releng aggregator source archive
evidence: The gzip/tar has 3502 members, including Eclipse documentation, build scripts, CI workflows and website generation. The flagged firstplugin_manifest.htm is a complete static Hello World tutorial, without executable scripts or an embedded object.

The exact instruction is to double-click plugin.xml to open the plug-in editor. The following escaped XML defines a HelloWorldView extension; it is a code listing, not executable HTML. The next paragraph explains the OSGi MANIFEST.MF editor tab.

Reviewed shell and workflow entry points perform Maven/build, Git maintenance, Eclipse test launches and official build-data downloads, consistent with the archive purpose. Every other original observation remains.
samples.limits: No signature or reproducible upstream archive identity was established. Attempts to retrieve the corresponding standalone Eclipse-common file from master/main returned 404; local content and execution context, not a claimed upstream byte match, establish this judgement.
samples.marker_line: Eclipse releng sources: BENIGN; editor tutorial, lure rule corrected

samples.identification: Modified XMRig x64 self-replicator with appended Go downloader and x86 Cobalt Strike Beacon
evidence: CRT entry 0x14009a338 -> 0x14009a1bc -> main 0x14002add4. Main opens argv[0] at 0x14002ae8c and reads its image. At 0x14002aee5 it reads two final DWORDs, decrements the first, and writes copies to randomized names under C:/Windows/System/.

0x14002af55 writes the self image; 0x14002af87 and 0x14002af9e write the updated generation/count DWORDs. 0x14002b01d launches each copy with CreateProcessW, then 0x14002b023..0x14002b03e loops to the supplied count. Actual footer values are 1463383815 and 171785553, both positive. File permissions, unchecked write failures and resource exhaustion can prevent completion; clone proliferation is still a concrete hostile implementation.

0x14002b043 onward enters the ordinary XMRig application flow. Its built-in CryptoNight cn/r pool is 3.120.209.58:8080, user/pass x, donate-level 0. These settings and Stratum references do not establish hostility on their own; the self-replication code and embedded backdoor tip the verdict.

Appended x86 Go PE at file 0xfc400: Go objdump resolves main.GetArchive at 0x58f220, net/http.Get at 0x58f2a2 and io.Copy at 0x58f323. Main downloads an S3 ZIP, extracts it via main.Extract and archive/zip, then joins C:/G DATA Security Software/ with AVK.exe and calls os/exec.Command at 0x58f0d3 and Cmd.Start at 0x58f0df. The non-admin branch constructs PowerShell Start-Process -Verb runAs and launches it. The original argv[0] self-replication path does not establish activation of this separate appended PE.

Appended x86 DLL at file 0x5b8601 exports _ReflectiveLoader@4. Loader 0x10008c79 finds its own PE, walks fs:[0x30] loaded modules, hashes module/export names with ROR13 and maps the image. The XOR-0x69 table at raw 0x2f228 decodes to typed Beacon settings: 5000 ms sleep, port 443, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top, HTTP transforms and rundll32 spawn paths.

DNS routines build cdn.%x%x.%s labels at 0x10002636 and chunked hex labels at 0x10003305, then call the DNS query routine through 0x100244c2 -> DnsQuery_A. The DLL also contains an operative task dispatcher at 0x10001000 and process creation paths. The DNS/reflective/config/hash findings describe actual code rather than only a family name.
samples.limits: Outer-to-Beacon and outer-to-Go activation links were not established. The configured endpoints were decoded, not contacted. No other malware-family names from the collector filename were used as evidence.
samples.marker_line: XMRig/Beacon carrier: MALICIOUS; clone proliferation and DNS backdoor

samples.identification: Unsigned launcher.dll dropping a Virut-infected WannaCry service
evidence: DllMain retains the module handle. PlayGame export at 0x1800011a4 builds C:/WINDOWS/mssecsvc.exe, calls the extractor at 0x180001014, then the hidden process launcher at 0x1800010f8.

The extractor loads resource W/101, reads a DWORD length, and writes resource+4 through CreateFileA/WriteFile (0x1800010d3). CreateProcessA at 0x180001178 uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW and hidden STARTUPINFO. This is the actual resource-to-file-to-execution path.

PE at file 0xc8a8 has an entry at VA 0xa6b121 inside an executable/writable .rsrc, diverted away from the original service startup. It validates a kernel image (0xa6b141..0xa6b16a), resolves hashed exports with multiply-by-15/subtract (0xa71854 onward), and contains the rolling byte decoder at 0xa7180d..0xa7182a (multiply, XOR, subtract and key exchange). The infector and Virut findings are supported.

Retained WannaCry main at 0x408140 calls InternetOpenUrlA at 0x408194. The result test at 0x4081a3 is followed by NOP/NOP at 0x4081a5..0x4081a6, then unconditional fall-through to the service path at 0x4081ad. It creates and starts mssecsvc2.0 at 0x407c9b..0x407cb2 with an auto-start type and Microsoft Security Center display name.

Nested PE at file 0x3e94c retains resource-archive extraction, WANACRY! header comparison at 0x401564..0x40157c and the t.wnry load/decrypt path. 0x40213a maps the recovered native image, resolves TaskStart at 0x40214b, and calls it at 0x402158. The encrypted-resource-payload identity is accurate.

The embedded password-encrypted ZIP has surviving local records for b.wnry, c.wnry, language ransom-message files, r.wnry and s.wnry, but no intact central directory. Its remaining bytes are damaged. No successful extraction, final TaskStart execution, victim file encryption or network spread is asserted.
samples.limits: This is a modified, damaged malware container, not an unmodified signed utility collected only because it could be abused. Original infection circumstances and runtime success remain unknown; hidden payload execution, a disabled safety branch and parasitic entry diversion independently support MALICIOUS.
samples.marker_line: WannaCry/Virut launcher: MALICIOUS; hidden dropper, infected payload

changes: Preserve the exact double-click text matcher and exclusions as a notable ui/help observation for non-PDF documents. In the current PDF pipeline there are no text strings for that matcher; add a disjoint PDF raw-byte observation of the same wording. A named any-composite supplies one instruction role. Neither observation claims visible text, execution or deception.

Require the instruction plus a native/script/JAR attachment in the same PDF or a confirmed executable in the same OOXML document for the suspicious document lure. Ordinary plugin.xml editor and installer instructions no longer imply an attack. Existing testing exclusions remain.

Relocate the two Stratum/pool-array composites from miner/smart to data/config/syntax and XMRig identity, preserving their conditions and platform/type scopes. Set notable severity because the required evidence establishes configuration/reference co-occurrence, not unauthorized use or protocol implementation. Remove unsupported cryptojacking ATT&CK/MBC mappings.

The only affected ancestor selector is CrystalX’s objectives/impact exclusion. Add the two relocated observations to its existing named exception group to preserve its exact exclusion population. No package-specific exceptions were introduced.
Retain every hostile finding on both malicious samples and all existing independent notable observations.

controls.outside_batch: Scanned original official XMRig 3.1.0 Windows release, existing native mining-only fixture, and existing WinRAR SFX/miner fixture before and after. Their findings and ML outputs are unchanged. The current malware sample retains all self-replication and Beacon attack findings.

sources.triage: The supplied Triage and MalwareBazaar pages were inaccessible through the web tool; no conclusions were drawn from sandbox scores.
sources.stock_miner: forager fetched https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/download/v3.1.0/xmrig-3.1.0-msvc-win64.zip; extracted xmrig.exe is an ordinary uncompressed native miner and has no self-replication code. The release and .forage.json are retained in scratch.
sources.document_fixture: Before narrowing the lure, searched its exact and ancestor YAML consumers and available fixtures. No existing fixture directly exercised its original wording rule. A forager-fetched Emotet OneNote from an external signature provides an additional real attack-document reference; its quoted View wording and unsupported file type do not match this old rule. No attack claim was erased on that basis; the complete original instruction observation is retained and the new attachment relationship is covered by inert PDF controls.

dependencies: No firing finding in this batch originated from a fetched dependency; no dependent-only exception was added.
material_losses: One unsupported double-click lure classification and two neutral Stratum/pool classifications cease firing as suspicious. Every original instruction/configuration matcher remains a notable observation in its correct home. No hostile finding, archive member or embedded PE coverage was lost. PDF plaintext instruction plus embedded-executable coverage was added.
classifier_disagreements: None at the final scan gate: Eclipse exits 0 with no hostile/suspicious findings; both malicious Windows samples exit 1 and remain on ML level 25. Raw ML probabilities are recorded, not treated as behavior evidence. Scans warn that the v18 model uses an older feature specification than extractor v19; this is an engine/model limitation outside YAML.
